newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia oilmen to meet ministers, prosecutor.
newsitem.headline: Colombia oilmen to meet ministers, prosecutor.

text.p: Colombia's main oil workers' union will restart talks with government ministers and the chief prosector Thursday in a bid to avert a threatened strike, union leader Hernando Hernandez said Wednesday.

No time had been fixed for the meeting by Wednesday evening but Hernandez said Interior Minister Horacio Serpa, Labor Minister Orlando Obregon and Chief Prosecutor Alfonso Valdivieso had agreed to meet a union delegation.
The union agreed a strike motion last Monday but the national directorate put the action on hold pending the outcome of negotiations, which began last Sunday.

The union is protesting the arrest of 14 men -- 11 of them members of the union -- in the last week, on charges of sabotaging oil pipelines and of links with the National Liberation Army (ELN), Colombia's second largest guerrilla force.
It is also objecting to what it sees as government plans for the creeping privatization of state-run oil company Ecopetrol.

"We will be demanding the immediate freedom of our jailed members and, if not, we will be threatening an indefinite strike when we meet Valdivieso. We're looking for a clear, fair and agile legal process in which the prosecutor will produce his evidence and we will offer proof of their innocence," Hernndez said.
He said he would be looking for further meetings with Mines and Energy Minister Rodrigo Villamizar to discuss future plans for Ecopetrol once the union had resolved the question of the detainees.

The union has avoided setting any start date for a walkout while talks are going on. Hernndez said members had started a slowdown but was unable to say what impact this had had on production. An Ecopetrol spokesman said all refining, production and transport activities were normal Wednesday.
